correctness.rationale: The claimed product follows directly from the planar Steiner area polynomial and the polar support integral; Santaló centering is forced by n-fold rotational invariance. Differentiation yields an exact expectation identity. For Z=sec(pi/n)cos U, the proof establishes Var Z<=sec^2(pi/n)(pi/n)^4/45 by a Lipschitz contraction, and mu(mu-1)/Var Z>81/16 using a fifth-order elementary tan inequality. This dominates the worst derivative covariance term because sup_{t>=0} t(t+2)^3/(1+t)^4=27/16. Endpoint values, positive inverse-square deficit, and fixed-offset n^-2 expansion follow by controlled Taylor expansions. Standard-library checker.py passed 560 finite checks; finite tests do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Mahler volume is a central affine invariant; Euclidean parallel rounding is a canonical geometric deformation of a polygon toward a disk. Known endpoint inequalities do not decide whether the product can reverse as the rounding radius increases. The all-n strict monotonicity and explicit positive inverse-square coefficient settle the complete radial path, while the fixed-offset n^-2 law quantifies the rate of the polygon-to-disk transition. This is a natural full-family ordering with sharp limits, rather than a small numerical improvement or a restatement of an endpoint bound.
